facts.statement: Leshansaurus lived during the Late Jurassic in what is now China.
facts.quote: Leshansaurus is a genus of theropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic Shaximiao Formation of what is now China.

facts.statement: Leshansaurus lived approximately 165 million years ago during the Bathonian stage of the Middle Jurassic in Asia.
facts.quote: Leshansaurus qianweiensis es la única especie conocida del género extinto Leshansaurus de dinosaurio terópodo sinraptórido que vivió a mediados del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 165 millones de años en el Bathoniense en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: Leshansaurus lived between 168.2 and 161.5 million years ago, spanning the Bathonian and Callovian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Bathonian to Callovian (168.2 to 161.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Leshansaurus was discovered in 2007.
Leshansaurus was named and described in 2009 by a team of Chinese paleontologists including Li Fei and Peng Guangzhao.
facts.quote: Leshansaurus qianweiensis was named and described in 2009 by Li Fei, Peng Guangzhao, Ye Yong, Jiang Shan, and Huang Daxi.

facts.statement: The name Leshansaurus qianweiensis honors the city of Leshan and the county of Qianwei in Sichuan, China, where the fossils were found.
facts.quote: The generic name refers to Leshan, a nearby city in Sichuan, China, and the specific epithet refers to Qianwei, the county in which the fossils were found.

facts.statement: Leshansaurus weighed approximately one tonne and stood about 1.5 to 2 meters tall at the hips.
facts.quote: Leshansaurus era un terópodo de tamaño mediano que habría tenido una longitud de entre 6 a 7 metros y una altura de cadera de aproximadamente entre 1,5 a 2 metros, con un peso de alrededor de 1 tonelada.

facts.statement: Leshansaurus possessed an elongated skull that was broader towards the front.
facts.quote: Leshansaurus has an elongated skull that is broader towards the front.

facts.statement: Unique features of Leshansaurus include a sharp ridge on the supraoccipital, elongated frontal bones, a horseshoe-shaped atlas intercentrum, and a distinct ridge on the inner side of the ilium.
facts.quote: Its autapomorphies (unique characteristics) are the possession of a sharp central ridge on the supraoccipital (the bone above the occipital), elongated frontal bones that are 2.86 times as long as they are wide, slender basipterygoid projections on the basisphenoid, a bone of the lower braincase, an atlas intercentrum that is horseshoe-shaped in cross-section, slender diapophyses, thin spines of the dorsal vertebrae and sacral vertebrae, the possession of a clear keel at the bottom of the sacral vertebrae, and an ilium with on the inner side a distinct ridge along the edge of the hip joint.

facts.statement: While originally placed in Sinraptoridae, Leshansaurus may actually belong to the family Megalosauridae.
facts.quote: Li et al. referred this taxon to Sinraptoridae – a group of carnosaurian theropods, but it may belong to Megalosauridae instead.

facts.statement: Leshansaurus is classified within the family Megalosauridae.
A 2012 analysis by Matthew Carrano placed Leshansaurus in the subfamily Afrovenatorinae as a sister species to Piveteausaurus.
facts.quote: Un análisis realizado por Matthew Carrano en 2012 descubrió que era miembro de Megalosauridae, dentro de la subfamilia Afrovenatorinae, como especie hermana de Piveteausaurus, un taxón conocido solo por una bóveda craneana casi idéntica la de Leshansaurus.

facts.statement: Leshansaurus fossils were found in the Shangshaximiao Formation, a geological layer known for its rich dinosaur fossil content.
facts.quote: Fossils of Leshansaurus were discovered in strata from the Shangshaximiao Formation, a formation rich in dinosaur fossils.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Leshansaurus belongs to the carnosaurian group Sinraptoridae or the family Megalosauridae.
facts.quote: Li et al. referred this taxon to Sinraptoridae – a group of carnosaurian theropods, but it may belong to Megalosauridae instead.

rejected.statement: The holotype skeleton includes a partial skull, lower jaws, numerous vertebrae, and much of the hind limbs and hands.
rejected.quote: The holotype (QW 200701) was found in 2007. It is a fairly complete skeleton consisting of a partial skull and lower jaws, seven cervical vertebrae, twelve dorsal vertebrae, five sacral vertebrae, two caudal vertebrae, and much of the hind limbs and hands.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'vertebrae and much of the hind limbs and'

rejected.statement: Leshansaurus was a medium-sized theropod reaching six to seven meters in length with a hip height of about 1.5 meters.
rejected.quote: Leshansaurus was a medium-sized theropod that would have had a length of six to seven meters, and a hip height of about one and a half meters.
